title: Canonical bidual of a dualizable object in a braided closed monoidal category
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with tensor $\otimes$, unit $\mathbf1$, associator $\alpha$ and unitors $\lambda,\rho$. Let $\sigma_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\otimes X$ be any braiding: a family of isomorphisms natural in $X$ and $Y$ satisfying both hexagon identities
$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ\sigma_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes\sigma_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(\sigma_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$
$$\alpha^{-1}_{Z,X,Y}\circ\sigma_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha^{-1}_{X,Y,Z}=(\sigma_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{X,Z,Y}\circ(1_X\otimes\sigma_{Y,Z});$$
no symmetry $\sigma_{Y,X}\sigma_{X,Y}=1$ is assumed. Assume $\mathcal C$ is closed on the right: for every object $L$ the functor $-\otimes L$ has a right adjoint $[L,-]$, with counit $\mathrm{ev}_{L,M}:[L,M]\otimes L\to M$, so that every $f:K\otimes L\to M$ has a unique transpose $f^\flat:K\to[L,M]$ with $\mathrm{ev}_{L,M}\circ(f^\flat\otimes1_L)=f$. Let $X$ be an object with a dual: an object $Y$ and morphisms $\eta:\mathbf1\to X\otimes Y$, $\epsilon:Y\otimes X\to\mathbf1$ with
$$\rho_X\circ(1_X\otimes\epsilon)\circ\alpha_{X,Y,X}\circ(\eta\otimes1_X)\circ\lambda_X^{-1}=1_X,\qquad \lambda_Y\circ(\epsilon\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{Y,X,Y}\circ(1_Y\otimes\eta)\circ\rho_Y^{-1}=1_Y.$$
Put $X^\vee=[X,\mathbf1]$ and let $b^\sigma_X:X\to[X^\vee,\mathbf1]$ be the transpose of $\mathrm{ev}_{X,\mathbf1}\circ\sigma_{X,X^\vee}:X\otimes X^\vee\to X^\vee\otimes X\to\mathbf1$. Then $b^\sigma_X$ is an isomorphism, for every such braiding $\sigma$ and every such $X$.

source.place: Tag 0FFP, definition-dual, and Tag 0FFQ, lemma-left-dual (Mor(Z'⊗X,Z)=Mor(Z',Z⊗Y) for a left dual Y of X), with Tag 0FFR, remark-left-dual-adjoint; the braided exchange of the two duality sides is the standard swap of an exact pairing.

proof.text: Put $D=[X,\mathbf1]$ and $v=\mathrm{ev}_{X,\mathbf1}$. For every $K$, the dual-pair formulas give inverse maps between $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Y)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(K\otimes X,\mathbf1)$: send $f$ to $\epsilon(f\otimes1_X)$, and send $g$ to $(g\otimes1_Y)(1_K\otimes\eta)$, inserting the unitors and associators of [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Indeed, applying the second after the first gives $(\epsilon\otimes1_Y)(1_Y\otimes\eta)f=f$ by the $Y$ triangle and bifunctoriality; applying the first after the second gives $g(1_K\otimes((1_X\otimes\epsilon)(\eta\otimes1_X)))=g$ by the $X$ triangle. These are direct substitutions into the two assumed identities.

source.place: Tag 0FFQ, lemma-left-dual, explicit mutually inverse Hom maps; Tag 0FFP, definition-dual. The right-closed chosen-evaluation identifications below are written out by the worker.

proof.text: Let $t:Y\to D$ be the transpose of $\epsilon$, so $v(t\otimes1_X)=\epsilon$. Set $s:D\to Y$ to $(v\otimes1_Y)(1_D\otimes\eta)$ with the same constraints. Step 1 gives $st=1_Y$. For $ts$, the transpose of $v$ is $1_D$, and the first inverse identity of step 1 gives $\epsilon(s\otimes1_X)=v$. Therefore the transpose of $v(ts\otimes1_X)$ is $ts$, and its value equals the transpose of $v$, namely $1_D$. Thus $ts=1_D$, and $t$ is an isomorphism. Transport the original exact pairing along $1_X$ and $t^{-1}:D\to Y$, using [lem-trf-exact-pairing-iso-transport]. The transported coevaluation is $a=(1_X\otimes t)\eta:\mathbf1\to X\otimes D$, and its evaluation is $\epsilon(t^{-1}\otimes1_X)=v$. Hence $(X,D,a,v)$ satisfies both triangles.

source.place: Tag 0FFQ, lemma-left-dual, explicit mutually inverse Hom maps; Tag 0FFP, definition-dual. The right-closed chosen-evaluation identifications below are written out by the worker.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-exact-pairing-braided-swap] to the exact pairing $(X,D,a,v)$. It gives an exact pairing $(D,X)$ whose coevaluation is $c=\sigma_{D,X}^{-1}a:\mathbf1\to D\otimes X$ and whose evaluation is $w=v\sigma_{X,D}:X\otimes D\to\mathbf1$. In particular $(1_D\otimes w)(c\otimes1_D)=1_D$ and $(w\otimes1_X)(1_X\otimes c)=1_X$, with constraints inserted. These are the two identities used below; no inverse braiding is replaced by a forward braiding.

Put $E=[D,\mathbf1]$ and $u=\mathrm{ev}_{D,\mathbf1}:E\otimes D\to\mathbf1$. By its definition in the statement, $b=b_X^\sigma:X\to E$ satisfies $u(b\otimes1_D)=w$. Define $k:E\to X$ by $(u\otimes1_X)(1_E\otimes c)$, inserting associators and unitors. Bifunctoriality gives $kb=(w\otimes1_X)(1_X\otimes c)=1_X$, by the $X$ triangle from step 3. Similarly, substituting the formula for $k$ and moving the disjoint tensor factors gives $w(k\otimes1_D)=u(1_E\otimes((1_D\otimes w)(c\otimes1_D)))=u$, by the $D$ triangle. Consequently $u((bk)\otimes1_D)=w(k\otimes1_D)=u$. Uniqueness of the transpose for $-\otimes D\dashv[D,-]$ yields $bk=1_E$. Thus $k$ is a two-sided inverse to the specified $b_X^\sigma$, proving the assertion.
